description: C++ programs for the Arduino Uno.

lessons.name: 01 Blink LED
lessons.description: Blink the built-in LED on the Arduino Uno.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Arduino Uno:
No external LED is required.

The built-in LED is connected to digital pin 13.

Upload the program to the Arduino Uno using the Arduino IDE.

lessons.name: 02 Button Input
lessons.description: Read a push button and control an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg of the button -> Arduino Uno D2
Other leg -> GND

The program uses INPUT_PULLUP, so no external resistor is required.

Built-in LED:
Arduino Uno D13.

lessons.name: 03 Buzzer
lessons.description: Make a buzzer produce a tone.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Active or passive buzzer:
Positive (+) -> Arduino Uno D8
Negative (-) -> GND

The buzzer will turn on and off every 500 milliseconds.

lessons.name: 04 Traffic Light
lessons.description: Control red, yellow, and green LEDs like a traffic light.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Red LED:
Anode (+) -> D8 through a 220 ohm resistor
Cathode (-) -> GND

Yellow LED:
Anode (+) -> D9 through a 220 ohm resistor
Cathode (-) -> GND

Green LED:
Anode (+) -> D10 through a 220 ohm resistor
Cathode (-) -> GND.

lessons.name: 05 Serial Monitor
lessons.description: Send messages and sensor values to the Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external connection is required.

Connect the Arduino Uno to the computer using USB.

Open Arduino IDE -> Tools -> Serial Monitor.
Set the baud rate to 9600.

lessons.name: 06 Analog Input
lessons.description: Read an analog value from a potentiometer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Potentiometer:
Left pin -> 5V
Middle pin -> A0
Right pin -> GND

The Arduino Uno will read a value from approximately 0 to 1023.

lessons.name: 07 LED Fade
lessons.description: Gradually increase and decrease LED brightness using PWM.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> Arduino Uno D9
Cathode (-) -> GND

D9 supports PWM and is used to control LED brightness.

lessons.name: 08 Light Sensor
lessons.description: Read a light-dependent resistor (LDR) using analog input.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LDR voltage divider:
LDR and a 10K resistor are connected as a voltage divider.

Divider output -> A0
Other side -> 5V and GND as appropriate for the divider.

Built-in LED -> D13.

The LED turns on when the measured light value is below 500.

lessons.name: 09 Button Counter
lessons.description: Count button presses and display the count in the Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> Arduino Uno D2
Other leg -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is enabled using INPUT_PULLUP.

Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud to see the counter.

lessons.name: 10 Button LED Toggle
lessons.description: Toggle an LED ON and OFF each time the button is pressed.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> Arduino Uno D2
Other leg -> GND

Built-in LED:
Arduino Uno D13

Each button press toggles the LED between ON and OFF.
